subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should the Codex WebSocket transport permanently use an unconditional 30-second opening-handshake cutoff and suppress error re-emission when no error listener is present?
rationale: The timeout value and terminal-event behavior affect existing slow connections and direct transport consumers; tests can prove mechanics but cannot choose the compatibility contract.

options.title: Bound timeout, preserve explicit errors
options.body: Keep the 30-second bound but retain predictable error delivery alongside exit, with callers and tests subscribing appropriately.

options.title: Accept the proposed event contract
options.body: Adopt the conditional error emission and rely on exit as the safe terminal signal for listener-light consumers.

options.title: Pause for transport policy design
options.body: Defer the patch until Codex transport timeout and terminal-event semantics are specified across all callers.

recommendation.title: Bound timeout, preserve explicit errors
recommendation.body: Keep the 30-second bound but retain predictable error delivery alongside exit, with callers and tests subscribing appropriately.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal ties this person to introduction and merging of the Codex app-server transport surface.
